newsitem.title: USA: Lowe's sees Q3 above estimates, Q4 below.
newsitem.headline: Lowe's sees Q3 above estimates, Q4 below.

text.p: Lowe's Cos Inc said on Thursday that it expects its third quarter earnings to be above Wall Street's expectations of $0.36 a share, but its fourth quarter results are expected to fall below estimates.
The retailer of home improvement products said earnings estimates of $1.63 for the fiscal year ending January 31, 1997 are "reasonable."
Shares of Lowe's, which also reported October sales results today, fell 5-1/8 to 38-3/8 on 1.67 million shares traded.
Analysts had a consensus fourth quarter earnings estimate of $0.32 a share for Lowe's.
Lowe's said strong sales of higher margin products such as plumbing, electrical, tools and home decorations have helped third quarter results.
Current trends in sales and margins to continue through the Christmas season, but its store opening costs are expected to be greater than the year ago period.
The number of stores to be opened is expected to exceed last year's fourth quarter, weather permitting, by 50 percent and those costs are expensed, Lowe's said.
Lack of achievement of annual bonus performance goals for stores and general office management in 1995 caused a 52-basis point expense reduction, the company said.
Lowe's said there is no restructuring reserve in 1996 to absorb relocation expenses.
Also, there was a LIFO inventory-related credit of $2.5 million in the fourth quarter of 1995 and that figure is undetermined for this year's fourth quarter.
